children.text: Observation Tool for Maths and Science Teachers (Grade VI- Grade VII)

FDE's tool for Maths and Science (Annexure G, pp.13-14), in 5 parts:

Part 2 · Before the lesson
1. Written work checked

Part 3 · During the lesson
2. Opening based on SLOs
3. Command on the content
4. Communication and delivery
5. Student-centric, activities

Part 4 · During the lesson
6. Supporting material
7. Links to daily life
8. Student assessment/questions
9. Wrapping up the lesson

Part 5 · After the lesson
10. Thinking outside the box
11. Management, differentiation

Part 6 · Student Assessment (5 students) and the development plan: Development area, Current level, Teacher goal, Action plan for the teacher

Each indicator is scored Level 0 to Level 3, in FDE's words.

err_note.__example__: Answer every item on this screen, then tap Next.

children.text: To change an earlier part, tap ← at the top. Your answers stay.
Assigning and checking written work including formative assessments (e.g. quizzes, monthly/ end of unit tests)

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Student notebooks show evidence of written work of the past 5 lessons assigned and checked by the teacher
Level 2: Along with level 1, regular written feedback has been provided by the teacher. Fellow students/ mentors have been assigned to check assignments as well
Level 3: Along with achieving level 2, formative (classroom) assessments have application-based questions that go beyond the simple copy/paste of the textbook

err_note.__example__: Answer every item on this screen, then tap Next.

children.text: To change an earlier part, tap ← at the top. Your answers stay.
A meticulous introduction/ opening provided based on specific Student Learning Outcomes (SLOs)

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Teacher begins with the current SLO and links it broadly to the topic.
Level 2: Teacher meets level 1 and links the SLOs to activities/tasks in class, and previous lessons or other subjects
Level 3: Along with level 2, introduction is provided to the topic with an exciting hook which could include either a short story, interactive activity, a fun fact or a thought-provoking question to the students
Effective teachers' command on the content/subject

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: The teacher can provide a lecture on the topic, however, she/he is unable to answer complicated questions from the students
Level 2: The teacher meets level 1 and can answer questions from students, however, he/she is unable to rephrase content depending on the needs of the students
Level 3: Teacher meets level 2, and is able to rephrase her/his content depending on the needs/ questions of the students. She/he can also discuss content that is not available in the textbooks

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Audible and coherent speech is delivered
Level 2: Along with level 1, the teacher has a friendly and positive body language, and engages all students through movement in class
Level 3: Along with level 2, the teacher uses engaging methods of delivery such as appropriate humour or short fun activities to grab the attention of the students

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Lesson has one activity performed by the teacher and majority of the lesson is lecture-based.
Level 2: Lesson includes one activity performed by students and activity is instructive and relevant to SLOs.
Level 3: Lesson includes several different types of activities performed by students and activities are instructive and relevant to SLOs. These activities are a combination of group, pair or solo activities.

err_note.__example__: Answer every item on this screen, then tap Next.

children.text: To change an earlier part, tap ← at the top. Your answers stay.
Use of supporting material (Visual or digital aids)

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Teacher effectively uses the black/ white board
Level 2: Teacher uses a visual aid which is instructive and relevant to SLOs
Level 3: Teacher uses several visual/digital aids of more than one type which are instructive and relevant to SLOs
Connections to practical examples or knowledge content from the students' daily lives

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Teacher gives 1 example of real-life application of SLO. The example is coherent with the students' prior knowledge and has a local context.
Level 2: Teacher gives 2 or more examples of real life application of SLO. Common misconceptions are dispelled.
Level 3: Teacher meets level 2 and asks students for examples of real life application scenarios
Student assessment/ questions (oral/ written) are asked

Level 0: Does not meet Level 1
Level 1: Teacher sets relevant questions to test understanding of only a few students.
Level 2: Teacher sets relevant questions and identifies correct and incorrect answers of most students.
Level 3: Teacher sets relevant questions before, during and after the lesson. She/he offers solutions for incorrect answers and positive praise for correct answers from all the students

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Teacher reiterates a broad topic covered during class and summarizes the SLOs
Level 2: Teacher meets level 1, and explains the connection to upcoming topics. Homework is assigned from the textbook and written on the board
Level 3: Teacher meets level 2, and assigns complementarily unofficial homework that is an inquiry-based activity outside of class

err_note.__example__: Answer every item on this screen, then tap Next.

children.text: To change an earlier part, tap ← at the top. Your answers stay.

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: An example/ activity was shared or provided that was not present in the textbook
Level 2: The teacher plans an activity or shares material not found in a typical classroom (e.g science kit)
Level 3: The teacher thinks beyond conventional, orthodox teaching methods to engage students with the lesson

Level 0: Does not meet level 1
Level 1: Teacher manages time well and maintains smooth transition of activities.
Level 2: Teacher meets level 1 and maintains a non-hostile learning environment. Teacher interacts with majority of the students in class, creating a dialogue
Level 3: Teacher modifies lessons to meet each student's individual interests, strengths, and needs (e.g those that lag behind the rest of the class).
